title: Interpersonal communication and subjective well-being of pregnant women: The role of communication channels
abstract: Context and relevance. Pregnancy is accompanied by significant changes, which can place women at risk of experiencing poor subjective well-being (SWB). Communication with close people has been recognized as an important factor in promoting psychological well-being, but there is a lack of research on how different aspects of communication and the nature of the relationship are related to social support (SS) and SWB for women during pregnancy with their first child. Objective: to study how the volume of communication and the structure of a social network (in terms of communication channels, degree of emotional closeness and social category of contacts) are related to three aspects of SWB (life satisfaction, well-being, richness of life). Hypotheses. SS, life satisfaction, and WHO-5 are associated with communication with emotionally close people, while richness of life is associated with communication with less close people. Face-to-face communication is associated with all indicators of SWB and SS during pregnancy. Methods and materials. The study involved 55 first-time expectant mothers at 3 to 8 months of pregnancy, working or studying at the time of the study (21—36 years old, M = 28 ± 4.4). An interview reconstructing a week-long experience of communication (directed communication) in three channels (calls, messengers, face-to-face). It also includes questions about the degree of emotional closeness of contacts on a scale from 1 to 10 and the social category of the contact. SWB was measured using the scales: WHO-5 — Index of general well-being, “Life satisfaction” by E. Diener and “Psychological richness of life” by S. Oishi, and the questionnaire of “Social support” by S. Cohen. Results. The results showed that computer-mediated communication, unlike face-to-face communication, does not have a positive effect on SWB and SS in pregnant women, with the exception of a positive effect on the richness of life. Conclusions. It is shown that the key importance for SWB is not the amount of communication, but their emotional closeness and channel of communication.
